cold_solve.reasoning: Stem window = 'before the wind drops'. The passage states the answer once: 'While the wind is still on the wall, it pushes in at those same joints, and the tray holds what it has collected.' D is a direct paraphrase (water already caught stays on the tray; the wind pressing IN at the joints is the reason) and adds nothing the text does not say. A is false twice: the wind 'pushes in', it does not force water out, and in the tested window the passage licenses no running joint at all. B is false twice: the outer skin 'wets through, as the specification assumes it will' and 'The water that gets past it runs down into the cavity, onto a tray', so water HAS reached the tray; and the perfect in 'holds what it has collected' presupposes completed collection, with enough on the tray to give back in the lull. C is true in its first conjunct and false in its second: the passage attributes the stoppage to the wind, raises the defect question only for 'a head that gives back nothing an hour after the wind drops', and says outright that 'an open joint cannot say' which defect it is. Key D confirmed, uniquely defensible; C is the strongest pull.
cold_solve.agrees_with_gkey_legs: Both verdicts-r3 G-KEY records (2 records, 0 kills, 0 flags) independently solve D on the same sentence.

findings.evidence: G-STEM r3: 'cavity-tray/weep-hole building pathology decides it for a domain reader. A/B/C are all substantive positions in that same domain (A = naive wind forces it out, B = absorption-lag, C = missing-stop-end, a real and common defect), so the passage is still doing real work. findings.claim: The unit's own blind-heuristic section does not derive the compound test-wise route that its own G-STEM leg found, and its net statement is scoped in a way that reads stronger than it is. G-STEM r3 derives a two-step narrowing to {C, D} at 50/50; the rationale derives five single-step heuristics, concludes 'the best any of them manages is a two-way between A and D', and never mentions a {C, D} pair.
findings.evidence: G-STEM r3 finding 3: 'Residual soft narrowing, form-adjacent only: on direction the set is 3-1 (A = joints discharging vs B/C/D = little or nothing discharging), and B is the only option that never names the joints the stem asks about, so a test-wise solver can shed A and B and sit at C-vs-D 50/50.' The rationale's (5) odd-one-out derives the same 3-1 direction split but only in the PICK-the-odd-one direction (returns A, a distractor); it never derives the SHED-the-odd-one direction, which is the more common test-wise move, and it never composes that shed with a second one. Its net sentence - 'no heuristic on this list returns D alone, and the best any of them manages is a two-way between A and D' - is literally true of the five listed heuristics but is not true of the route space, since a {C, D} two-way exists and G-STEM found it.
findings.why: This is the same shape as the defect that refuted the unit at rounds 1 and 2 - a blind-answerability claim in the unit's own text that is narrower than the claim a reader takes from it - though it is now a scoping issue rather than a false conclusion, and the residual it hides is a 50/50 rather than a delivery of the key. It is a minor rather than a blocker for three reasons: the route terminates in domain knowledge by G-STEM's own analysis ('deciding C vs D needs the stem presupposition... and that step requires knowing what a stop end is, i.e. domain, not form'), so it collapses into the already-dispositioned N1; the residual pair contains C, which every leg and this audit's cold solve independently rate the strongest distractor, so the 50/50 is a genuine 50/50 and not a disguised tell; and the route is disclosed in the gate record that travels with the batch.
findings.disposition: SHIP with the residual recorded here. Cheapest remedy if a later stage wants it: one sentence in the rationale's heuristic (5) deriving the shed-direction and naming the {C, D} terminus, with the same domain-not-form disposition G-STEM gave it. No option, key, stem or passage edit is implied, and none should be made - arming B with the word 'joints' to break the second shed would simultaneously worsen N2.
